newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan business mood hurt by tax, but to improve - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan business mood hurt by tax, but to improve - MOF.

text.p: Japan's corporate sentiment worsened in May, hit by a tax rise in April, but it is likely to recover gradually, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said in a survey released on Wednesday.
"Business sentiment worsened temporarily in May, but is expected to recover gradually," said a MOF official who briefed reporters on the results of the survey.
He added that the rise from April 1 in the national consumption tax to five percent from three percent was one factor behind the deterioration in sentiment.
The ministry released two surveys covering businesses, one on sentiment for May and the other on their activities during the January-March quarter.
Both surveys covered Japanese firms capitalised at 10 million yen or more, excluding financial institutions and insurance firms.
The MOF official said business sentiment was expected to improve, taking into account strong capital spending data.
The January-March survey showed that capital spending by the firms had risen 13.0 percent from a year ago, the strongest growth since the July-September quarter of 1990, when it rose 16.9 percent.
Capital spending has shown year-on-year increases for eight consecutive quarters, the official said.
The firms' current profits for the January-March period also rose for the 11th quarter in a row, increasing 18.2 percent from the previous year.

"Corporate earnings continue to improve on the back of strong capital spending," the official said, adding that economic recovery centring around private demand would become more clearly evident in the future. -- Tokyo Policy Desk +81-3-5473-3710
